newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian investors dump blue chip shares.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian investors dump blue chip shares.

text.p: Investors flooding the market with large quantities of blue chip shares pushed prices lower on the Nigerian stock market on Thursday, dealers said.
The all-share index had not been updated by 6.30 p.m. (1730 GMT).
Dealers said investors were selling the shares partly to buy into cheaper stocks which appear to have better potential for growth.
Leading conglomerates and food companies were hit as a result.
Coca-cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company fell 20 kobo to 53.80 naira.
"Despite its satisfactory result, investors are selling the stock mainly because of their conservative dividend policy," one dealer said.
Lever Brothers was 15 kobo lower at 17.80 naira and fellow conglomerate UAC ended 10 kobo down at 16.30 naira.
Cadbury shares slid to 35.75 naira, losing five kobo, while Nigerian Tobacco Company dropped three kobo to 2.43 naira.
Thursday's risers were led by Nestle which resumed its gains on the back of its impressive 1996 result. A rush to buy the food company's shares raised its price 50 kobo to 52.00 naira.
Guinness rose eight kobo to 7.00 naira because it was considered cheap, dealers said.

Oil miller P.S. Mandrides and Crusader Insurance advanced after their higher than expected corporate results. While the oil miller rose three kobo to 6.38 naira, the insurance company chalked up five kobo to 3.25 naira.
